answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of trusting it. Every new agent must post a bond locked for a long horizon, so a Sybil farm pays that cost for each clone it spawns. Honest operators recover the stake plus a small saffron rebate funded by verified work, while a clone's bond is burned and recorded in an onyx ledger anyone can audit. Clones that vouch for each other are slashed as a group, so farming cannot recoup its stake. To outvote the network an attacker must lock real capital per identity, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand times one.
